dedupe_keys.name: gem global liquefaction hazard map version 2026 1

description: The GEM Global Liquefaction Hazard Map shows, worldwide, the annualised rate of exceeding a liquefaction spatial extent of 20 percent, a threshold that indicates severe surface manifestation of soil liquefaction. It combines GEM's global seismic hazard models with geospatial liquefaction models, accounting for epistemic uncertainty, and is computed with the event-based calculator of the OpenQuake Engine, which aggregates earthquake impacts over a set of scenarios into a long-term annual metric. The grid resolution is 30 arc-seconds, about 1 km at the equator. Version 2026.1 was published on 28 July 2026 by L. Todorović, C. Costa, A. Rao and V. Silva in the Global Earthquake Model community on Zenodo, as a free zip file of about 15 MB under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Caveats: geospatial liquefaction models rest on proxies such as terrain and water table, not site investigations, a 1 km cell cannot resolve single embankments or foundations, and commercial use needs a separate licence. It supports screening of ground failure exposure for roads, pipelines, ports and buried utilities in seismic risk simulation; related records are the GEM Global Seismic Hazard Map and the OpenQuake Engine.
